arrival.note: A BOUND FROM THE RETURN, NOT AN ARRIVAL. The office's list of letters uncalled-for is a RETURN — its statement of what was still unclaimed on ONE day — and the paper reprinted one return over as many consecutive issues as it took, so the bound is dated by the return of June 1835 and not by the issue it was read in (T-0425). The earliest issue this project reads the name in is 1835-07-01, 1 day later; that gap is an accident of which impression an extraction pass reached, and it is not evidence. Somebody was writing to this name at Chicago by 1835-06-30 and at no stated time before it; nothing says when they came. The date lines the printings set, and how they were weighed, stand beside this rule in tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py.

persons.note: PROJECTED RESIDENT. Documented in Chicago post-office evidence but not independently corroborated strongly enough for attested circa-1835 residence. KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN. The papers print 'Gabbs, James I1.' in a single return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 1 July 1835, column 5 — dated 1835-07-01. AN INITIAL THIS PROJECT CANNOT READ, MARKED AS ONE. The card shows 'James [?] Gabbs': the scan sets a DIGIT where the middle initial goes, and a digit is never part of a name, so the character is carried as [?] — the marker the Chicago list of 1 January 1834 already uses for an initial the printing did not deliver. NO LETTER IS SUPPLIED. The deposit holds two transcriptions of this issue and no page image, and the alternate carries no letter list at all, so there is no cleaner impression here to settle it against and the project declines to guess (T-0721; the suspicion is registered, ungraded, at data/research/residents/letter_list_reading_suspicions.json). The verbatim setting is untouched and quoted above; what has stopped is the card asserting that setting is a name. A pass that reaches the page images settles it and this marker goes. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). No figure is drawn (L1).

merge_ruling.for_merge: One interior vowel, 'James' identical, and both cards come from the post office inside one town. 'Gabbs' is set nowhere in the deposited corpus.
merge_ruling.against_merge: THE CARD'S OWN READING IS A BRACKETED UNKNOWN. It is 'James [?] Gabbs' — the middle initial was not read, and T-1027's table prints the underlying line as 'Gabbs, James I1.', which is type damage and not a name. The Gibbs card carries a definite middle initial H from the return of 20 May 1835 (#c013). A reading with an unread name-part cannot be compared at that part, so C9's first condition can be neither met nor refuted, and the fold would supply the letter it is supposed to be testing. R5, and T-0695 owns the image.

research_note: MINTED FROM THE LETTER LISTS (T-0378, T-0379). THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER, NOT AN ARGUMENT: every other record here argues for a household, and this one argues for a PERSON. `data/residents/` cannot carry a person outside a household, so one was written around them and told to claim nothing — one member, no dwelling, no division, no trade, no family, no arrival beyond the paper's bound. tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py derives the set and prints every refusal, `--gate` proves no record here gained a roof, a trade or a second member, and docs/LIBERTIES.md L214 carries the change of scale.
